background: UniCredit is Italy's second-largest bank and a leading lender in Germany, Austria and Central and Eastern Europe, funded by deposits across those markets, with a large stake in Commerzbank and a Russian subsidiary it has been winding down.
synthesis: The bank is rated A- on average across all three main agencies, none of them lower, with one on a positive outlook and two on a stable outlook; the last move was a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 25 Nov 2025. Capital is on the weak side of EU and Nordic banks: CET1 of 14.2% is below the peer median and has fallen 2.1 points since 30 Jun 2024, and leverage of 5.2% is below the median too. Liquidity is mixed, with LCR of 141% in the bottom quarter and NSFR of 124% at the median. The newest flagged item, on 27 Jul 2026, concerns an EU sanctions exemption that could help close its stalled Russian disposal, alongside an earlier profit beat as its Commerzbank stake nears a majority.
